action: A small black-line butterfly starts on the hand beside the gray butterfly, grows larger in frames 2-4, then jumps left and shrinks while one of its wing outlines stretches into a long loose stroke that trails behind and slowly fades away.
identity_gap: The wings do not stay closed and attached to the body. From frame 2 on, one wing outline comes loose and becomes a long open stroke across the frame, so the two-lobed wing pair that defines the doodle is lost. The curly antennae and tick-marked body do carry over.
notes: Frame 1 reads clearly as the doodle at small scale, but after that the drawing comes apart: the body line stretches, one wing becomes a huge separate curve, and the figure jumps from the hand to the left edge between frames 4 and 5. By frame 7 the butterfly is a small squashed mark and the stray stroke is the main thing on screen.
